records.statement: The two-sample t-test for unpaired data targets a difference between two population means using two independent samples.
For unpaired mean comparison without an equal-variance assumption, NIST uses the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom and notes robustness to unequal sample sizes and/or unequal variances.
The pooled two-sample t form is a special case when equal variances are assumed; NIST gives the simpler pooled degrees of freedom when equal variances are assumed and sample sizes are similar.
Data are paired when each observation in one condition is naturally matched to the corresponding observation in the other condition; paired analysis is performed on the within-pair differences.
The paired-sample t-test uses the mean and standard deviation of the within-pair differences and tests the mean difference using N minus 1 degrees of freedom.

The ordinary fixed-effect ANOVA model assumes errors are independent, normally distributed with mean zero, and have equal variance; the model assumptions concern errors rather than simply the raw response values.

ANOVA model adequacy should be assessed with residual diagnostics, including residual patterns against fitted values and observation order, normality assessment, outlier checks, and variance-pattern assessment; transformations may be considered when residual patterns indicate nonconstant variance or nonlinearity.
Repeated measurements on the same experimental unit cannot be assumed independent and require the statistical model to account for correlated errors.

When factor levels are sampled from a larger population rather than fixed by the researcher, the factor is random and the model and hypothesis tests differ from ordinary fixed-effect ANOVA; mixed models combine fixed and random effects.
records.section: Lesson 6 Random Effects and Introduction to Mixed Models

records.statement: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is a paired-data procedure based on the signs and magnitudes of ranked within-pair differences and requires the population distribution of differences to be symmetric about the target median.
records.section: 6.5 A Nonparametric Alternative: The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test

records.statement: The Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney procedure should not be interpreted generally as a test of equality of medians. Divine et al. formulate the tested quantity as Pr(X1 < X2) + Pr(X1 = X2)/2, with null value 0.5.
A pure location-shift interpretation of Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney requires stronger distributional assumptions; differences in shape or variance undermine a simple median/location interpretation.
records.section: 2.3 What Does the WMW Test Do?

records.statement: Kruskal-Wallis is a rank-based nonparametric procedure for comparing several independent samples/populations when a parametric distributional model is not being assumed.
